summary: Create a knowledge-graph governed-state surface for mapping key concepts, their definitions, and relationships between them across Xavier's projects and domains.
rationale: Without a canonical concept map, Claude cannot reliably connect ideas across sessions. The same term may be used differently in BrewMind vs. a research thread vs. a build project, leading to inconsistent reasoning. More importantly, as Xavier builds knowledge over time — reading, researching, experimenting — there is no durable place for that knowledge to live. Supabase captures raw thoughts (Tier C), but a governed concept map holds structured, owner-verified knowledge (Tier A/B). This surface enables: (1) defining terms Xavier uses consistently (e.g., what 'BrewMind' means in scope, what 'session' means in governance context); (2) tracking relationships between concepts (e.g., BrewMind -> uses -> memory-policy; research-methodology -> informs -> proposals); (3) identifying knowledge gaps (concepts referenced but not yet defined); (4) giving Claude a stable vocabulary to reason from rather than re-deriving definitions each session.
proposed_diff_summary: Create users/cici/governed-state/knowledge-graph/ directory with two artifacts: (1) concept-schema.json — JSON schema for a concept entry: fields include id (slug), label, domain (string: e.g. 'brewmind', 'governance', 'research', 'personal'), definition (Xavier-verified short definition), aliases (alternate names), related_concepts (array of concept ids), tier (A/B/C, indicating how verified the definition is), updated_at; (2) concepts.json — initial concept map seeded with ~10 core concepts already in use across the repo (cici, governed-state, memory-policy, proposal, evidence-tier, brewmind, open-brain, session-start, hypothesis, synthesis). Update surface-map.json to add knowledge-graph as a new active surface.
